questiontext.text: Which definition best matches containment?

answer.text: The strategy of limiting the expansion of Soviet influence rather than attempting immediate rollback everywhere.
A policy that ended all international conflict immediately.
A military event unrelated to this lesson.

questiontext.text: What was the central goal of containment?

answer.text: To prevent further expansion of Soviet influence
To restore Axis governments
To end all American alliances
To annex Western Europe

questiontext.text: How did the Marshall Plan support containment?

answer.text: Economic recovery was intended to strengthen European stability and reduce the appeal of communism.
It supplied atomic weapons to every European country.
It ended all trade with Europe.
It required Western Europe to join the Soviet bloc.

questiontext.text: What did the Berlin Airlift demonstrate?

answer.text: The Western Allies could resist pressure and sustain West Berlin without directly attacking Soviet forces.
The Allies abandoned West Berlin.
Germany was reunified in 1948.
NATO dissolved before it was created.

questiontext.text: Why was NATO historically significant?

answer.text: It committed member states to collective defense and marked a lasting U.S. security role in Europe.
It was a temporary wartime rationing agency.
It transferred Western Europe to Soviet control.
It ended the Korean War before it began.

questiontext.text: How did the Korean War test containment?

answer.text: The United States and United Nations intervened after North Korea invaded South Korea, seeking to resist expansion without starting a wider world war.
It was fought to restore Japanese rule in Korea.
It caused the immediate dissolution of the Soviet Union.
It involved no international forces.
